main_text.p: sententiam, exA Act.19.30. historia fit verisimile. Cæterum Bellarminus calumniosè tractat Magdeburgenses, quos ait Paulum reprehedere: quum illi manifestò testentur se ambigere an reprehendendus sit. Calumniosius, quòd censuras tales, si minus veras, at modestas, & veri studio adhibitas, perstringit horribilium blasphemiarum nomine. Quid enim? b Epist.89.ad Augustin.Hieronymus affirmavit Paulum in Petro reprehendendo egisse simulatè, non serio: nec sensisse, quod scripsit, eum non rectè incessisse advèritatem Evangelii. Hìc errasse Hieronymum evincitc Epist.19.ad Hieron. Augustinus Pauli testimonio:d Gal.1.10. In iis quæ scribo vobis, ecce coram Deo loquor, no mentior. Ete In epist. ad Gal. cap.2. leg.3. Aquinas statuit veriorem esse opinionem Augustini, quàm Hieronymi, quia cum dictis Apostoli magis concordat. Sed num Hieronymus horribilem in Paulum blasphemiam effudisse propterea judicandus est? Itemf De agone christian. ca. 30. Augustinus simulationem in Petro reprehensam appellat, & pravam: ac inter gravia Petri crimina recensèt. In quo, utg De Rom. Pont. lib.1. cap.28. Bellarmino Augustinus displicet: sic &h Biblioth. sanct. lib.6. annot.274. Sixto Senensi. Sed Sixtus de eo ait, Videtur Petrum durius tractasse quàm par sit: num Bellarminus dicet, horribiliter blasphemavit? Deniquei In enarrat. psal.13. Chrisostomus,k Homil. de occursu Dom. Amphilochius,l In Evang. Luc. cap.2. Theophylactus, gladium de quo Simeon Virgini Mariæ,m Luc.2.35. Tuam, inquit, animam pertransfibit gladius, exponunt de scandalo dubitationis, in quam inciderit tempore passionis Christi. Atqui dolorem significarin Psal.22.21. gladio probabilius est: Papistis certè sic persuasum dubitationem non significari, ut expositionem eam explodato De Maria Virg. lib.4. cap.27. Canisius lesuita, velut exp Homil.17. in Lucam. Origenis amaro fonte promanantem. Sed num Theophylactum, Amphilo-chium,

page.notes: Marginal note marks o and p are doubtful: the printed margin mark for "De Maria Virg." reads as a rounded p/o, and the Canisius and Origenis marks in the text are hard to tell apart. The text sentence "Sed num Theophylactum , Amphilochium," ends at the last full line, and the word Amphilo-chium is split at the line end with its printed hyphen. A small stray mark at the lower left of the page is not printed text and is not transcribed. The running head is read as "De Romanæ Ecclesiæ idololatriâ" with the final letters uncertain.
